The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ have the standard product presentation, smooth structure, and period-one basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of the upstream torus definition. Use its selected product Milnor model $ET=(E_{S^1})^r$ with the right diagonal action and $BT=ET/T$. For a smooth left $T$-manifold $X$, define real Borel equivariant cohomology by $H_T^*(X;\mathbb R)=H^*(ET\times_T X;\mathbb R)$ using the quotient convention $(e\cdot t,x)\sim(e,t\cdot x)$. Its coefficient ring is $\mathcal R=H^*(BT;\mathbb R)\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)=\mathbb R[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, where $u_i$ is the class corresponding to the dual period-one basis vector $e_i^*$ and each $u_i$ has degree $2$.

For an integer vector $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)$, write the character as $\chi_m(t)=\exp(2\pi i\sum_i m_i t_i)$ and define its degree-two class by $u_{\chi_m}=\sum_i m_i u_i$. With the stated quotient convention, this is the Euler class of the Borel line $ET\times_T\mathbb C_{\chi_m}$, where $T$ acts on $\mathbb C_{\chi_m}$ by $\chi_m$. Use the complex-orientation convention $c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line $L$; thus $u_\chi$ is also the first Chern class of its Borel character line. Let $S\subset\mathcal R$ be the multiplicative set generated by these classes for all nontrivial characters, together with $1$; thus $u_\chi\ne0$ exactly for nontrivial $\chi$. Write $S^{-1}H_T^*(X;\mathbb R)$ and $S^{-1}\mathcal R$ for the corresponding localizations. The coefficient-ring identification is used under AC: the upstream classifying-space cohomology proof invokes AC in its Künneth and coefficient arguments.

If $X$ is a compact oriented smooth $T$-manifold without boundary of dimension $n$ and the action preserves its orientation, the Borel projection $\pi_X:ET\times_T X\to BT$ has compact oriented $n$-dimensional fibers. Define equivariant integration $\int_X\alpha=(\pi_X)_!\alpha$, the cohomological pushforward along those fibers; it lowers degree by $n$ and has values in $\mathcal R$. For an oriented $T$-equivariant vector bundle $E\to X$ whose Borel-associated bundle has a normalized Thom class, define its equivariant Euler class $e_T(E)$ as the pullback of that Thom class by the zero section. The Thom class is normalized to restrict on each oriented fiber pair $(D^c,S^{c-1})$ to the positive generator of $H^c(D^c,S^{c-1};\mathbb R)$. For rank $c=0$, the Thom class and Euler class are $1$. For a complex representation line of character $\chi$, this convention gives Euler class $u_\chi$. For a fixed component $F$ of a $T$-action on $M$, the orientation convention is $o(TM|_F)=o(TF)\wedge o(\nu_F)$, where $\nu_F$ is its chosen equivariantly oriented normal bundle. This is the Borel convention; no identification with a Cartan, Chow, or quotient-stack cohomology model is assumed here.

Assume AC. Let \(r\geq0\), let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) use the product Milnor model \(BT=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r\) with its ordinary product topology, and let \(F\) be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Then \(BT\times F\) is paracompact Hausdorff and has the homotopy type of a CW complex. In fact, there is a finite CW complex \(K\) such that \(BT\times F\simeq BT\times K\).

For a well-pointed topological group $G$ of CW type, the diagonal action on Milnor's $EG$ is free, $EG$ is contractible, and

$$ p:EG\longrightarrow BG $$

is a numerable principal $G$-bundle. The numeration satisfies the library's support-subordinate convention, not merely cozero containment.

The embeddings

$$e\left(\sum_i t_i g_i\right)=\sum_i t_i g_i\text{ in slot }2i,\qquad o\left(\sum_i t_i g_i\right)=\sum_i t_i g_i\text{ in slot }2i+1$$

are $G$-equivariantly homotopic to the identity. If $a,b:T\to EG$ are
continuous equivariant maps, then
$(1-t)e(a(-))+t\,o(b(-))$ is a continuous equivariant homotopy.

For $G=S^1$ or $G=\mathbb Z/2$, the selected compact-group topology identifies $BG$ with the standard weak CW colimit of the finite projective quotients $\mathbb{CP}^N$ or $\mathbb{RP}^N$, respectively.

Assume AC.  Every $R$-oriented rank-$n$ numerable vector bundle over a CW
complex, or over a paracompact Hausdorff base of CW type, has a unique
normalized Thom class $u_\xi$, and
$$a\longmapsto\pi^*a\smile u_\xi:H^k(B;R)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^{k+n}(D(\xi),S(\xi);R)$$
for every $k$.  Without a supplied orientation, the canonical twisted form is
$$H^k(B;\mathcal O_R(\xi))\xrightarrow{\cong}H^{k+n}(D(\xi),S(\xi);R).$$
The finite supplied-trivializing-cover theorem is a choice-free special case.

derivations.claim: Average any Riemannian metric on $M$ over normalized Haar measure on $T$ to obtain a $T$-invariant metric. The normal exponential map is $T$-equivariant; its derivative is invertible along the zero section, so the inverse function theorem and compactness of $N$ give a $T$-invariant tubular neighborhood identified with $\nu$. Since $T$ fixes $N$ pointwise, $ET\times_T N\cong BT\times N$, and the Borel normal bundle $ET\times_T\nu$ is an oriented rank-$c$ vector bundle over the CW space $BT\times N$.

The Borel principal bundle $ET\times N\to BT\times N$ is the pullback of the selected product Milnor bundle. If $r=0$, this is the trivial principal bundle over a point; otherwise, for each circle factor, [F3] supplies a numerable trivializing cover and subordinate partition. Products of these finitely many covers and partition functions are locally finite and subordinate to product principal-$T$ charts. Pulling the numeration back to $BT\times N$ shows that the associated Borel normal bundle $ET\times_T\nu$ is numerable. It is oriented by the given $T$-invariant orientation. By [F2] its base is paracompact Hausdorff of CW type, so [F4] gives the normalized Thom class $\tau_\nu$ and the cup-product isomorphism in every degree.

Use the tubular-neighborhood identification and excision to transfer $\tau_\nu$ to $H_T^c(M,M\setminus N;\mathbb R)$. For each $\beta\in H_T^*(N;\mathbb R)$, define $i_*^T(\beta)$ as the image of the cup product of this relative Thom class with the pullback of $\beta$ under the relative-to-absolute map $H_T^*(M,M\setminus N;\mathbb R)\to H_T^*(M;\mathbb R)$. This canonical composite is the Gysin map and is defined for every $\beta$ by the Thom isomorphism.

Pull the relative class in step 3.1 back along the zero section. By the definition of $e_T(
u)$ in [F1], the pulled-back Thom class is $e_T(
u)$, and pullback respects cup products. Hence $i^*i_*^T( eta)=e_T(
u)\smile eta$.

The Gysin class in step 3.1 is represented in a tubular neighborhood of $N$. Choose such neighborhoods disjoint for disjoint compact fixed components $N,N'$. The representative restricts to zero on $N'$, so $i_{N'}^*i_{N*}^T(\beta)=0$.

In the tubular-neighborhood representative from step 3.1, integrate first along each oriented normal disk fiber. The Thom class integrates to $1$ by its fiber normalization, so this fiber integration returns $\beta$ on $N$; the orientation convention in the Statement makes the resulting base orientation the one used by $\int_N$.

Equivariant integration over $M$ factors in the tubular neighborhood into integration over the normal fibers followed by integration over $N$. Step 4.3 therefore gives $\int_M i_*^T(\beta)=\int_N\beta$. These identities establish every stated Gysin property.

derivations.claim: Average a Riemannian metric over normalized Haar measure on $T$. At $p\in F$, the exponential map of this invariant metric is $T$-equivariant and is injective on a sufficiently small ball in $T_pM$. Thus, for $v$ in that ball, $\exp_p(v)$ is fixed by every $t\in T$ exactly when $v$ is fixed by every linear map $d_pt$; the fixed set near $p$ is the exponential image of $(T_pM)^T$. Therefore $F$ is locally a smooth submanifold and $T_pF=(T_pM)^T$. The fixed locus is closed in compact $M$, hence compact; its connected components are open in this locally connected manifold and compactness gives only finitely many.

The orthogonal complement of $(T_pM)^T$ in $T_pM$ is the normal fiber, so it contains no $T$-fixed vector. The complexification of an orthogonal representation of the abelian group $T$ is a commuting family of unitary maps and decomposes into simultaneous character eigenspaces; complex conjugation pairs the $\chi$ and $\bar\chi$ spaces. A real one-dimensional character would have image in $\{+1,-1\}$ and is trivial because $T$ is connected. Thus every nontrivial real summand is two-dimensional. Averaging the representation against each character gives smooth projections onto the finitely many weight subbundles along each $F_j$.

If $
u_j$ has nonzero weights, choose $X\in\mathfrak t$ outside the finite union of their kernels. For a character $\chi$, define the real linear weight $\omega_\chi(X)$ by $\chi(\exp(sX))=\exp(2\pi i s\omega_\chi(X))$. On its real weight subbundle the infinitesimal action $A_X$ satisfies $A_X^2=-(2\pi\omega_\chi(X))^2I$, so $J_\chi=A_X/(2\pi\omega_\chi(X))$ is invariant and satisfies $J_\chi^2=-I$. Their direct sum gives an invariant complex structure on $
u_j$. Its complex orientation may agree or disagree with the chosen normal orientation, with comparison sign $\epsilon_j$. The weight projections vary continuously, so their ranks, and therefore the character multiplicities, are constant on connected $F_j$. If there are no weights, then $
u_j=0$ and the complex structure is vacuous.

The torus acts trivially on $F_j$, hence $ET\times_TF_j\cong BT\times F_j$ and the Künneth isomorphism over $\mathbb R$ gives $H_T^*(F_j;\mathbb R)=H^*(F_j;\mathbb R)\otimes\mathcal R$. Restrict $e_T(\nu_j)$ to any point of $F_j$. The normal representation is the direct sum of the complex character lines in step 3.1; the Euler class of a direct sum is the product because the product of the normalized Thom classes restricts to the positive generator on each direct-sum fiber and hence is its normalized Thom class. By [F1] each line has Euler class $u_{\chi_{j,a}}$, and the orientation comparison gives $f_j=\epsilon_j\prod_a u_{\chi_{j,a}}$ as the degree-zero-in-$H^*(F_j)$ component. Every factor is nonzero and belongs to $S$, so $f_j$ is a unit in $S^{-1}\mathcal R$.

Write $e_T(\nu_j)=f_j+n_j$, where $n_j$ has positive degree in $H^*(F_j;\mathbb R)$. Since $F_j$ is compact of finite dimension, every product of sufficiently many positive-degree cohomology classes vanishes; choose $N$ with $n_j^N=0$. In the localized ring the inverse is $f_j^{-1}\sum_{q=0}^{N-1}(-f_j^{-1}n_j)^q$, since multiplying by $f_j+n_j=f_j(1+f_j^{-1}n_j)$ telescopes to $1-(-f_j^{-1}n_j)^N=1$. If $c_j=0$, $n_j=0$ and $f_j=1$, giving the empty-product case as well.

derivations.claim: Localize the restriction map $i^*:H_T^*(M;\mathbb R)\to H_T^*(F;\mathbb R)$ at $S$. By [L2] it is an isomorphism in this compact smooth finite-type case. Let $\beta=i^*\alpha=(\beta_j)_j$ under $H_T^*(F)=\bigoplus_jH_T^*(F_j)$.
By [F3], each $e_T(\nu_j)$ is invertible after localization. Form $\gamma=\sum_j i_{j*}^T(\beta_j/e_T(\nu_j))\in S^{-1}H_T^*(M;\mathbb R)$; the sum is finite because $F$ has finitely many components.

All maps and identities in [F2] are $\mathcal R$-linear and extend $S^{-1}\mathcal R$-linearly to the localized modules. For a component $F_\ell$, pull back $\gamma$. The $j=\ell$ term is $e_T(
u_\ell)\, eta_\ell/e_T(
u_\ell)= eta_\ell$ by the localized self-intersection identity; each $j
e\ell$ term restricts to zero by the localized disjoint-support identity. Hence $i^*\gamma= eta=i^*\alpha$. Since the localized restriction map in step 1.1 is injective, $\gamma=\alpha$.

The $\mathcal R$-linear pushforwards in [F1] and the identity $\int_M i_{j*}^T(\delta)=\int_{F_j}\delta$ in [F2] extend $S^{-1}\mathcal R$-linearly, so they apply to $\delta= eta_j/e_T(
u_j)$. Applying $\int_M$ to step 3.1 gives $\int_M\alpha=\sum_j\int_Mi_{j*}^T( eta_j/e_T(
u_j))=\sum_j\int_{F_j} eta_j/e_T(
u_j)$, which is the fixed-component formula in the localized coefficient ring. If $F=\varnothing$, [L2] says $S^{-1}H_T^*(M)=0$, so $\int_M\alpha$ localizes to zero; because $\mathcal R$ is a domain and every element of $S$ is nonzero, $\mathcal R\hookrightarrow S^{-1}\mathcal R$ is injective and the empty sum is indeed zero. If a normal rank is zero, its Euler denominator is $1$ by [F3], so that term is the ordinary integral over that fixed component.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ have the standard product presentation, smooth structure, and period-one basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of the upstream torus definition. Use its selected product Milnor model $ET=(E_{S^1})^r$ with the right diagonal action and $BT=ET/T$. For a smooth left $T$-manifold $X$, define real Borel equivariant cohomology by $H_T^*(X;\mathbb R)=H^*(ET\times_T X;\mathbb R)$ using the quotient convention $(e\cdot t,x)\sim(e,t\cdot x)$. Its coefficient ring is $\mathcal R=H^*(BT;\mathbb R)\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)=\mathbb R[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, where $u_i$ is the class corresponding to the dual period-one basis vector $e_i^*$ and each $u_i$ has degree $2$.

For an integer vector $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)$, write the character as $\chi_m(t)=\exp(2\pi i\sum_i m_i t_i)$ and define its degree-two class by $u_{\chi_m}=\sum_i m_i u_i$. With the stated quotient convention, this is the Euler class of the Borel line $ET\times_T\mathbb C_{\chi_m}$, where $T$ acts on $\mathbb C_{\chi_m}$ by $\chi_m$. Use the complex-orientation convention $c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line $L$; thus $u_\chi$ is also the first Chern class of its Borel character line. Let $S\subset\mathcal R$ be the multiplicative set generated by these classes for all nontrivial characters, together with $1$; thus $u_\chi\ne0$ exactly for nontrivial $\chi$. Write $S^{-1}H_T^*(X;\mathbb R)$ and $S^{-1}\mathcal R$ for the corresponding localizations. The coefficient-ring identification is used under AC: the upstream classifying-space cohomology proof invokes AC in its Künneth and coefficient arguments.

If $X$ is a compact oriented smooth $T$-manifold without boundary of dimension $n$ and the action preserves its orientation, the Borel projection $\pi_X:ET\times_T X\to BT$ has compact oriented $n$-dimensional fibers. Define equivariant integration $\int_X\alpha=(\pi_X)_!\alpha$, the cohomological pushforward along those fibers; it lowers degree by $n$ and has values in $\mathcal R$. For an oriented $T$-equivariant vector bundle $E\to X$ whose Borel-associated bundle has a normalized Thom class, define its equivariant Euler class $e_T(E)$ as the pullback of that Thom class by the zero section. The Thom class is normalized to restrict on each oriented fiber pair $(D^c,S^{c-1})$ to the positive generator of $H^c(D^c,S^{c-1};\mathbb R)$. For rank $c=0$, the Thom class and Euler class are $1$. For a complex representation line of character $\chi$, this convention gives Euler class $u_\chi$. For a fixed component $F$ of a $T$-action on $M$, the orientation convention is $o(TM|_F)=o(TF)\wedge o(\nu_F)$, where $\nu_F$ is its chosen equivariantly oriented normal bundle. This is the Borel convention; no identification with a Cartan, Chow, or quotient-stack cohomology model is assumed here.

Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let $T$ be a compact torus acting smoothly on a compact oriented smooth $n$-manifold $M$ without boundary; use the standard Hausdorff, second-countable manifold convention, and assume the action preserves the orientation. Write $F=M^T=\coprod_{j=1}^{s}F_j$ for its fixed locus, with $s<\infty$, and $i_j:F_j\hookrightarrow M$ for each connected component. Give each normal bundle $\nu_j$ a $T$-equivariant orientation and orient $F_j$ by $o(TM|_{F_j})=o(TF_j)\wedge o(\nu_j)$. Use real Borel equivariant cohomology, $\mathcal R=H^*(BT;\mathbb R)$, the multiplicative set $S$ generated by nonzero character classes, and the degree-shifting fiber-integration convention of the preceding definition. For every homogeneous $\alpha\in H_T^k(M;\mathbb R)$,

$$\int_M\alpha=\sum_j\int_{F_j}\frac{i_j^*\alpha}{e_T(\nu_j)}\quad\text{in }S^{-1}H^{k-n}(BT;\mathbb R).$$

If the fixed locus is isolated, use the ambient orientation on each normal space $\nu_p=T_pM$ and the positive orientation on each point $p$. Necessarily $n=2m$. Choose a $T$-invariant complex structure on each $T_pM$ and let $\chi_{p,1},\ldots,\chi_{p,m}$ be its nonzero character weights. Let $\epsilon_p=+1$ when its complex orientation agrees with the orientation of $M$ at $p$ and $-1$ otherwise. Then the same formula specializes to

$$\int_M\alpha=\sum_{p\in M^T}\frac{\epsilon_p\,i_p^*\alpha}{\prod_{a=1}^{m}u_{\chi_{p,a}}}\quad\text{in }S^{-1}\mathcal R.$$

This is a finite-dimensional formula for compact manifolds; it does not assert a formula for arbitrary noncompact instanton spaces or infinite-dimensional field spaces.

derivations.claim: A point $[z_0:z_1]$ is fixed by every $\lambda$ precisely when it lies on one coordinate axis, so the fixed set is $\{p_0,p_\infty\}$. In the coordinate $w=z_1/z_0$ near $p_0$, the action is $w\mapsto\lambda w$, giving tangent weight $+1$; in $v=z_0/z_1$ near $p_\infty$, it is $v\mapsto\lambda^{-1}v$, giving weight $-1$. The complex orientations agree with $M$, so the Euler denominators are $u$ and $-u$.

The tautological fiber at $p_0$ is the trivial coordinate line, and at $p_\infty$ it is the weight-$+1$ coordinate line. Dualizing gives the fixed-fiber weights $0$ and $-1$ for $\mathcal O(1)$, hence $x|_{p_0}=0$ and $x|_{p_\infty}=-u$.
Substituting these restrictions and tangent Euler classes in [F2] gives $\int_M x=0/u+(-u)/(-u)=1$.

The linear functional $\ell(z_0,z_1)=z_0$ defines a section of $\mathcal O(1)$ that vanishes only at $p_\infty$. In the local coordinate $v=z_0/z_1$ and the dual tautological frame there, its coefficient is $v$, so its unique zero is transverse with positive local degree $+1$. Pulling the normalized Thom class back by a transverse section counts its isolated zeros with these local degrees: excision reduces the pairing to the degree of the section on the boundary of a small disk around each zero. Hence the ordinary Euler number is $1$. Restricting the Borel pushforward to the basepoint of connected $BT$ gives this ordinary Euler number, and $H^0(BT;\mathbb R)=\mathbb R$; therefore $\int_{\mathbb{CP}^1}x=1$, independently confirming the localized sum.

derivations.claim: The first-factor action fixes exactly $p_0=[1:0]$ and $p_\infty=[0:1]$, while it fixes every point of the second factor. Thus $M^T=F_0\sqcup F_\infty$, with each component a copy of $\mathbb{CP}^1$. The normal bundle is the tangent line of the first factor at its fixed point; in the coordinates $z_1/z_0$ and $z_0/z_1$ its weights are $+1$ on $F_0$ and $-1$ on $F_\infty$.

The normal complex line is the first factor and the fixed-component tangent space is the second. Moving the real two-dimensional first-factor orientation past the real two-dimensional second-factor orientation has sign $(-1)^{2\cdot2}=+1$, so the induced component orientations agree with the product orientations.

The dual tautological fiber at $p_0$ has weight $0$ and at $p_\infty$ has weight $-1$, so the first-factor class restricts to $0$ and $-u$. Thus the contribution from $F_0$ is $0/u=0$; on $F_\infty$, the restricted class is $(-u)\eta$ and the normal Euler class is $-u$, leaving $\eta$, whose integral is $1$. The fixed-component sum is therefore $1$.

Product fiber integration factors over the two compact oriented factors. On the first $\mathbb{CP}^1$, the section of $\mathcal O(1)$ induced by $\ell(z_0,z_1)=z_0$ has one positive transverse zero at $p_\infty$, so its Euler integral is $1$ by the normalized Thom-class zero count; the second-factor integral of $\eta$ is $1$ by definition. Hence $\int_M\alpha=1\cdot1=1$, agreeing with step 3.1.
